articles.headline: Could the Big Ten turn to NFL-style scheduling model? Ohio State AD Ross Bjork hints at change
keyFacts: Ohio State athletic director Ross Bjork stated that the Big Ten is considering a results-based scheduling model similar to the NFL.
Bjork explained that the proposed dynamic model could begin in 2028, with future opponents determined by previous season rankings while protecting key rivalries.
Bjork noted that the change is being discussed to address increased roster parity across the conference created by NIL and the transfer portal.
body: The Big Ten has already adopted what amounts to a salary cap in college athletics, and now it might take another step toward mimicking the NFL with its approach to scheduling. Ohio State athletic director Ross Bjork said the conference is looking at a results-based scheduling model.

Bjork joined "The Ryan Day Show" on 97.1 The Fan and shared some insight about discussions around scheduling. Bjork noted that -- when the Big Ten first expanded to include the West Coast teams -- scheduling rotations were based upon historical records in football.
Well, teams like Indiana are in a very different place now than they were even five years ago.
"They looked at historical rotations over the course of everyone's football life," Bjork said. "Indiana was not what Indiana is today when they set the model. Same thing with UCLA."

Bjork said changes could begin with the 2028 season, explaining that opponents wouldn't be set in stone until after the 2027 campaign. The Big Ten would use a dynamic scheduling model, like the NFL's, based on the previous season's results. Worse teams would get more favorable slates. Better teams would get tougher matchups.
The one major difference is that the Big Ten would ensure key rivalries, like Ohio State vs. Michigan, remain in place every year.

"So, next year's schedule, we would not know who we're playing, other than protecting the rivalry games," Bjork said. "Obviously, we have the biggest one. Other than that, the rest of the schedule could be based on how the teams finished the previous year. That's how the NFL does it."

Bjork said a new model is required due to the parity created by NIL and the transfer portal. A dynamic scheduling model could be a more equitable way to balance strength of schedule across the league.
"We're having active conversations that we need to change the way we schedule," Bjork said. "... There's a lot more parity in the system."

One potential flaw in adopting the NFL's model is that current transfer portal and NIL rules allow limitless player movement every offseason. That creates much more volatility from one season to the next, unlike in the NFL, where multi-year contracts create more roster stability.
It's an intriguing idea, though, and scheduling will be a hot topic with the 24-team College Football Playoff arriving soon.

articles.headline: Tatsuya Imai reportedly will exercise player option, return to Astros after rocky first season in MLB
keyFacts: Pitcher Tatsuya Imai reportedly will exercise his $18 million player option to return to the Houston Astros for the 2027 season.
During his first MLB season, Imai faced injuries and command issues, pitching 76 2/3 innings with a 4.93 ERA.
Imai struggled to adapt to the American lifestyle, travel, and MLB pitching mounds after moving from Nippon Professional Baseball.
body: This season with the Houston Astros, right-handed Japanese pitcher Tatsuya Imai showed glimpses of what made him so special in Nippon Professional Baseball, a league where he became a three-time All-Star.

He even threw six spotless innings on May 25, spearheading a combined no-hitter against the Texas Rangers. But a 2026 campaign that began with him getting roughed up in his first MLB start and then saw him join a collection of Astros pitchers on the injured list raised serious questions about whether his arm will make him a lasting starting pitcher in the bigs.

Imai, who eventually was demoted from Houston’s starting rotation, is hoping for a better 2027, which he reportedly will spend with the Astros as well. The 28-year-old righty will exercise his $18 million player option and return to the team, according to multiple reports Thursday .
Last winter, Imai signed a three-year deal with the Astros reportedly worth up to $63 million, with $54 million of that money guaranteed .

He wound up pitching just 76 2/3 innings, posting a 4.93 ERA along the way. Imai made only eight appearances over the final two months of the season. Notably, he didn’t pitch in either of the Astros’ wild-card losses to the Chicago White Sox.
When Imai was on the IL with arm fatigue this spring, Imai confessed that he was struggling to adapt to the American lifestyle, both on and off the diamond.
When asked back then what was difficult outside of baseball, Imai provided an example via an interpreter.

“For example, the travel is different from Japan,” Imai said at the time, in mid-April, per The Athletic’s Chandler Rome . “The timing when the players eat. In Japan, when they get back to the hotel, they eat their dinner. Here, the players eat at the stadium.”

Earlier in the season, he complained that the Seattle Mariners’ mound was hard and voiced that he wasn’t used to pitching in cooler temperatures — that was after he gave up four walks and three runs while recording one out at T-Mobile Park.
Even before that, he talked about the challenge of adjusting to the mound slope in MLB.

But, again, there moments of promise, like when he piled up nine punchouts against the Athletics in his second start, a bounce-back performance . In June, he stitched together back-to-back starts with 10-plus Ks, one versus the Cleveland Guardians and the next against the Detroit Tigers.

Imai’s command issues plagued him the most. He walked six batters per nine innings. Going forward, he’ll need to improve his pitch location, and perhaps his pitch diversity, to regain a bigger role with the Astros.

articles.headline: Xavier Becerra’s ‘immigrant’ story thrust back into spotlight in embarrassing interview slip
keyFacts: Xavier Becerra faced criticism during an interview after describing his background as a son of immigrants despite his father being born in Sacramento.
Conservative Latino activists accused Becerra of pandering, while his campaign spokesperson defended his family history as typical for immigrant families.
Becerra leads Republican rival Steve Hilton by 24 points ahead of the November election, according to a new poll.
body: Dem frontrunner Xavier Becerra leaned into his identity when asked what changes he would bring as California governor — but the exchange quickly grew awkward after he was asked to clarify his origin story.
The candidate suddenly broke into Spanish when he was asked by KCRA how he’d be different from his predecessor, Democratic Gov. Gavin Newsom, if elected.
“That’s one of the biggest differences, actually, who I am and what I bring,” Becerra said in English after flexing his Spanish-speaking ability.
“If you want to know where a leader is going to take you, know where they’ve come from,” he elaborated further. “I don’t know if we’ve ever had a governor who comes from where I come from.”
The former Health and Human Services secretary seemed to be alluding to the fact that he’d be the first Latino elected governor in modern history. California is roughly 40% Latino.
But the reporter chimed in: “Sacramento?”

“Well I come from — born and raised in Sacramento, but I mean in terms of my roots, my background, son of immigrants, working-class family, parents who never had a chance to step into a college classroom,” Becerra clarified.
He then concludes his answer by saying, ultimately, what matters is that “I am my own person.”

The awkward moment, however, was seized upon by critics who had raised red flags over his family background. Becerra has portrayed his late father as an “immigrant” despite the father being born in Sacramento.

Becerra’s campaign has dismissed the criticisms and shared details of his father’s life, where the elder Becerra, who died in 2020, was born in Sacramento in 1928 as the eldest of eight children, according to an online obituary.
His family then moved back to Mexico when he was a child, living in Tijuana before he returned to California as a teen. Becerra’s mother was born in Mexico.
Becerra spokesperson Jonathan Underland said it’s not uncommon in immigrant families for individuals to temporarily move back to their parents’ home countries.

But conservative Latino activists and organizations have blasted Becerra over his repeated description of himself as the son of immigrants who arrived in the US with $12, with some even calling it “immigrant stolen valor.”

“That’s why he tried to act like his parents were from over there because he’s trying to pander to the Latinos,” Jesse Holguin, a former Los Angeles-area gang leader from La Puente, said to The Post. “He just thinks that’s gonna make him sound more Latino to them, and they’re gonna be like, ‘Oh yeah, he’s a real Latino, and he’s really for us.’”
Becerra is currently leading in the polls just a few days away from the November election.

A new poll by the Public Policy Institute of California has Becerra, with 61% of likely voters, dominating his Republican rival Steve Hilton, at 37%, by a 24-point margin. Hilton immigrated to the U.S. from the United Kingdom.

articles.headline: GM reaches $220M settlement over selling drivers’ private data
keyFacts: General Motors agreed to pay $220 million to 36 states to settle allegations that it illegally sold private driving behavior and location information to data brokers.
The multi-state settlement requires GM to obtain drivers' express consent before collecting or sharing data and mandates a third-party compliance assessment.
GM stated that the agreement addresses its Smart Driver product, which was discontinued in 2024, and reinforced its commitment to privacy protections.
body: General Motors will pay $220 million to 36 states to settle allegations that it illegally sold private driving behavior and location information to data brokers.

As part of the settlement, GM must get drivers’ express consent before it collects or shares their driving and location data — terms that are in line with separate agreements it previously reached with California and the Federal Trade Commission. This settlement does contain a new requirement that GM must have a third-party assess the automaker’s compliance with the privacy program it has put in place.

The agreement announced Thursday settles a lawsuit brought by a coalition of attorneys general from 36 states that alleged GM had sold the information to data brokers, which in turn then sold it to insurance providers.

“This agreement addresses Smart Driver, a product we ended in 2024, and reinforces steps we’ve taken to strengthen our privacy practices,” GM said in an emailed statement. “Safer, more helpful and personalized experiences are enabled by connected vehicle data, and GM is committed to being clear about what information is used, how it’s protected, and the choices customers have about what they share.”

The settlement comes more than two years after a New York Times report showed how GM and OnStar collected, used, and sold drivers’ precise geolocation data and driving behavior to third parties, including data brokers LexisNexis and Verisk. The data was collected through GM’s Smart Driver program, a free feature contained within its connected car apps that tracked and rated driving behaviors and seatbelt use. Data brokers sold this information to insurance providers, which could affect customers’ rates, the NYT reported at the time.

GM discontinued Smart Driver in 2024, but that didn’t stop legal action. In January, the FTC finalized an order that bans GM and its OnStar telematics service from sharing certain consumer data. The FTC settlement, as well as the multi-state one announced Thursday, also requires GM to be more transparent with its consumers and receive their explicit consent for certain collection.

GM now says it is focused on protecting the privacy of its customers and will no longer sell vehicle information that can be linked to an individual, their vehicle location, or how they drive. However, GM may still disclose anonymized data not tied to an individual with certain partners. GM has also updated the language in its privacy policy and created a consumer-facing Privacy Center.

GM’s settlement and mandated changes to how it handles customer driving data come as more sensor-laden vehicles equipped with computing power enter the market. Automakers have made large bets on software-centric vehicles that drivers and passengers can interact with and connect with other digital apps such as their calendar, messages, and email.

GM, for instance, is adding a personal AI assistant to OnStar, its 30-year-old safety and roadside assistance service. Cameras on the vehicle will be connected to the software to offer live views as well as crash and safety recordings. Users will also be able to use voice to control certain functions on the vehicle, including climate, and ask questions about any specific vehicle feature.

The automaker emphasized its privacy protections when it announced the new assistant during its GM Forward event in October. The company said customers will have the ability to decide what data is shared and that the recordings have time limits and are encrypted. GM said it and OnStar cannot access Connected Camera recordings. Customers will also be able to manage permissions. However, customers who opt not to share their data will likely have limited access to certain features, according to GM.

articles.headline: Patrick Stewart, best known for "Star Trek" and "X-Men," dies at 86
keyFacts: Actor Sir Patrick Stewart died at age 86 at home on Wednesday following dementia, his spokesperson confirmed.
Stewart was best known for playing Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek, Charles Xavier in X-Men, and award-winning stage roles.
Stewart reprised his role as Charles Xavier in the film Avengers: Doomsday, which will be released in December 2026.
body: Legendary actor Sir Patrick Stewart, best known for his work in the "Star Trek" and "X-Men" franchises and his prolific award-winning stage career, has died at 86 years old, his spokesperson confirmed.
Stewart died at home on Wednesday, spokesperson Kelly Bush Novak said in a statement. His death followed "a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia," Novak said.

"He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter, and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all," Novak said.
Stewart began his acting career doing stage plays in the United Kingdom, joining the Royal Shakespeare Company in the 1960s.

Stewart's most recognizable role began in 1987, when he started playing Enterprise Captain Jean-Luc Picard on "Star Trek: The Next Generation." The show ran for seven seasons and also spawned four "Star Trek" films featuring Stewart as Picard and the rest of the "Next Generation" cast. Stewart later reprised the role for Paramount+ series "Star Trek: Picard," which ran for three seasons.

Fellow "Star Trek" legend William Shatner posted: "Sir Patrick Stewart was a friend, a colleague, and a magnificent actor. From the stage to the bridge of the Enterprise, he brought intelligence, grace, and a deep sense of humanity to everything he did. Captain Picard stood for the best of us, and so did the man who played him. I was filled with affection and admiration for him and his work."

Stewart also played X-Men leader Charles Xavier in over half a dozen films in the "X-Men" franchise. He reprised the role for the upcoming "Avengers: Doomsday," which will be released in December 2026. Marvel Studios said on social media that it was "deeply saddened" by Stewart's passing, calling him a "singular talent" who defined the character "for generations of fans."

Stewart appeared in dozens of other film and television roles, including voice work on Seth MacFarlane's animated shows "Family Guy" and "American Dad." But the bulk of his work was on the stage: He was a frequent presence on Broadway and in London's West End, where he played characters from Shakespearean villains to Charles Dickens' Ebenezer Scrooge. He appeared with "X-Men" co-star Ian McKellen in "Waiting for Godot" in London in 2010, then again in New York City in 2013. He also performed his one-man version of "A Christmas Carol" frequently over the decades.

Stewart appeared in over 60 Royal Shakespeare Company productions. The company named him an "Honorary Associate Artist" to celebrate his contributions to their work. He has also been awarded three Olivier Awards for his London stage performances and received one Tony nomination for his work on Broadway.
Stewart was nominated for multiple Emmy, Golden Globe and SAG awards for his on-screen roles. He won a Grammy Award in 1995 for "Best Spoken Word Album for Children."
In 2001, Queen Elizabeth II appointed Stewart an Officer of the Order of the British Empire. In 2010, Stewart received a knighthood, again from Elizabeth II, for his services to drama.
In 2023, Stewart published the memoir "Making It So." The book landed him on the New York Times' best-sellers list. He also recorded a companion audiobook.

Stewart was actively working until 2026. In addition to his role in "Avengers: Doomsday," he recorded an audiobook where he narrated and commented on all 154 of William Shakespeare's sonnets. He also had a voice role in the animated comedy "The Sheep Detectives."

Stewart was married three times. He wed Sheila Falconer in 1966. The pair had two children — Daniel and Sophia — before divorcing in 1990. From 2000 to 2003, he was married to producer Wendy Neuss. In 2008, he began dating singer-songwriter Sunny Ozell. The two married in 2013 and were wed until his death. Novak said Ozell was at Stewart's side when he died.

Stewart was also "a fierce advocate for causes he strongly believed in," his spokesperson said. Those causes included social justice, women's rights, domestic abuse advocacy, veterans' rights, the refugee crisis, animal rights and political reform.

"We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace," Novak said. "His sonorous voice and singular talent will forever be synonymous with indelible performances in every genre. … He will be remembered for the dignity, compassion and humanity he brought to every role — in his art and life."

Vice-President JD Vance offered to restart nuclear diplomacy with Iran in exchange for sanctions relief, according to a report.
Donald Trump directed US officials to allow defeated Brazilian candidate Flávio Bolsonaro into the country, reports stated.
body: Trump again calls for prosecution of Mary Peltola as turmoil grows over Alaska campaign investigation – live
‘This is voter fraud at the highest level,’ president tells rally crowd in South Carolina; Alaska governor orders inquiry into Peltola campaign amid Republican outcry
On the campaign stage in South Carolina, Trump again calls for prosecution of Mary Peltola
Speaking to a campaign audience in South Carolina, Donald Trump reiterated his belief that Mary Peltola should be criminally prosecuted and disqualified from the Alaska Senate contest.

“This is voter fraud at the highest level,” Trump said of the Peltola campaign’s alleged scheme to recruited a man who shared the name of her Republican opponent, Dan Sullivan, to run, all in a bid to peel away votes.
Trump added that Peltola “should be removed from the ballot and prosecuted, and so should the fake Dan Sullivan”.
“I think it’s a criminal act, what they did,” Trump said.
JD Vance writes to top Iranian security official in sign Washington has not abandoned diplomacy
Patrick Wintour

Hopes of averting a major new conflagration between Iran and the US soon after Tuesday’s midterm elections could rest on Iran’s response to a personal letter from the US vice-president, JD Vance, offering to restart diplomacy.

The letter, written after predominantly Qatari mediation, was sent to the secretary of Iran’s supreme national security council, Mohsen Rezaei, on Sunday. It requires Tehran to agree to make commitments on its nuclear programme at the start of a process that would lead to the opening of the strait of Hormuz within seven days in return for US sanctions relief.

A reply is imminent, but Iran is reluctant to give upfront and irreversible commitments on its nuclear programme, such as exporting its stockpile of highly enriched uranium to a third country, if the compensatory US steps, such as lifting sanctions on Iranian oil exports, are reversible.

Republicans escalated calls to investigate Mary Peltola’s alleged ballot-stacking scheme. Donald Trump, JD Vance and other Republicans echoed the president’s calls to criminally investigate Peltola for recruiting a man with the same name as her opponent to join the Alaska Senate race.

Alaska’s governor went one step further, ordering an investigation into Peltola. “Deliberately tricking voters into casting their ballots for someone else strikes at the integrity of our elections,” Mike Dunleavy, the governor, said in a post on X. “Anyone or any organization found to have broken the law must be held accountable.”

A new CNN poll found that Democrats are leading Senate races in Texas and Michigan. The poll found that James Talarico and Abdul El-Sayed led by a significant margin over their Republican opponents. But it turned up no clear leader in Maine, once thought a likely Democratic pickup, or Kansas, a deep red state where the race has turned unexpectedly competitive.

New reporting indicates Trump aided Flávio Bolsonaro’s flight from Brazil to the US. According to the New York Times, the president ordered Bolsonaro, the defeated right-wing candidate for Brazil’s presidential election, to be allowed into the US on temporary status. A White House official also arranged the flight that brought Bolsonaro to Miami.

Trump, campaigning today in South Carolina, canceled another planned rally in Kansas. The president opted not to appear in-person at a rally in Kansas on Saturday, instead opting to focus on participating in remote tele-rallies. Other slated campaign appearances in Florida and Iowa are set to continue as planned.
Trump ditches plan to attend Kansas rally in Saturday
President Trump has canceled one of his last scheduled campaign stops before the midterm elections next week, axing his plans to appear at a rally in Kansas.

The planned stop in Salina, Kansas, would’ve come as Republicans seek to fend off a surprise challenge from Democrat Adam Hamilton, who polls have found could flip the normally deep-red seat currently held by incumbent Roger Marshall.
Instead of appearing in Kansas, Trump will instead partake in a remote tele-rally for Marshall.
Trump’s other slated appearances through the weekend – including one in Florida and another in Iowa – are still expected to go ahead as planned.
New Mexico’s Deb Haaland poised to be first female Native American governor
With a comfortable lead in the polls, Deb Haaland, a former congresswoman and interior secretary under Joe Biden, is set to become the first Native American woman to serve as governor in US history.

Her campaign has energized New Mexico’s Indigenous communities. But while the historic nature of her potential victory isn’t lost on her, Haaland says the hectic final stretch of her campaign has pushed it to the back of her mind.

“Sometimes I forget about the fact that I would be the first Native woman,” Haaland said in a recent interview. “We’re in the throes of this statewide campaign and it’s so busy and we’re trying to be everywhere all at once.”
My colleague Cecilia Nowell has the story in New Mexico:
Trump, speaking to a crowd in South Carolina, mused about continuing his habit of unilaterally renaming bodies of water with the strait of Hormuz, the Hudson River and the Atlantic Ocean.

During his second term, Trump has attempted to rebrand the Gulf of Mexico and Lake Ontario as the Gulf of America and Lake America, respectively. Since the outbreak of war with Iran, Trump has vowed to see the strait of Hormuz, the vital maritime shipping route for oil and gas that Iran has strangled in retaliation, renamed the “Trump Strait”.
“Now I need a river and an ocean,” Trump said.

Musing on which rivers he would rename, Trump said: “The only two I could think of were the Hudson River and the Mississippi.” He added: “I guarantee you, I will never be changing the name of the Mississippi.”
(No word yet on why the Potomac, Colorado or Ohio rivers, among others, weren’t suitable candidates.)
On the campaign stage in South Carolina, Trump again calls for prosecution of Mary Peltola
Speaking to a campaign audience in South Carolina, Donald Trump reiterated his belief that Mary Peltola should be criminally prosecuted and disqualified from the Alaska Senate contest.

“This is voter fraud at the highest level,” Trump said of the Peltola campaign’s alleged scheme to recruited a man who shared the name of her Republican opponent, Dan Sullivan, to run, all in a bid to peel away votes.
Trump added that Peltola “should be removed from the ballot and prosecuted, and so should the fake Dan Sullivan”.
“I think it’s a criminal act, what they did,” Trump said.
Trump is now speaking onstage at a midterm rally in Rock Hill, South Carolina

He’s in the state to campaign on behalf of Senator Darline Graham, the sister of late Senator Lindsey Graham who was appointed to finish his term. She finds herself in a surprisingly close race with Democratic nominee Annie Andrews.

So far, Trump has – among other remarks – defended the war in Iran and his economic record, waxed nostalgic about his debate performance against Joe Biden, and called for cognitive tests for elected officials (while touting his own record of taking such tests).

He also went on an extended tangent attacking the reliability of pollsters. This as Republicans face dismal polls that put Democrats ahead in several key Senate races (though the polls have underestimated Trump before).
Trump aided Bolsonaro's flight from Brazil to US, New York Times reports

Flávio Bolsonaro, the rightwing candidate who clandestinely fled Brazil for Miami after losing the Brazilian presidential election, planned his escape with the blessing of the Trump administration, the New York Times reported on Thursday.

The paper, citing US officials familiar with the plan, said that Trump had ordered that Bolsonaro be welcomed into Florida on a temporary parole status, which will probably be extended to permanent residency. A White House official also arranged the private jet that shuttled Bolsonaro and his family to Miami, the Times reported.

Bolsonaro fled Brazil after his losing the election in a come-from-behind victory for the left-wing incumbent, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who had also unseated Bolsonaro’s father, Jair Bolsonaro, in 2022. Jair Bolsonaro, once one of Trump’s strongest allies in Latin America, is now serving a 27-year sentence for allegedly trying to unseat Lula in a coup.

Flávio Bolsonaro picked up his father’s torch, running on a right-wing platform to unseat Lula. After his defeat, he was ordered to surrender his passports in connection with a criminal money laundering investigation.
Instead, Bolsonaro absconded across the border with Argentina alongside his family, flight from there to Ecuador and ultimately to Florida.
Trump did not outright endorse Flávio Bolsonaro in the race. But he has an increasingly embittered relationship with Lula, and has said that the results in the Brazilian election appeared rigged.
From his new home in Florida, Flávio Bolsonaro has declared himself the true winner of the election and vowed to contest the results.

For months, Donald Trump and others accused Peltola and Democrats of recruiting candidates with the same name as her Republican opponent, Dan Sullivan, to purposefully confuse voters when they cast their ballots in next week’s midterms.
Though Peltola’s campaign denied encouraging or soliciting a man named Dan J Sullivan to run, a recent New York Times report indicated Peltola’s campaign did recruit him.

While ballot stacking is not illegal itself, the US president and justice department have filed a lawsuit pre-emptively to block the certification of the Senate election results if the incumbent senator loses.
In this explainer, my colleague Ariana Baio takes you through what to know about the situation and ballot-stacking.
Senate race in once reliably Republican South Carolina tied in final stretch – poll
Joseph Gedeon

A US Senate race in one of the most Republican states in the country is now a dead heat, according to a new poll showing Democrat Annie Andrews tied with Darline Graham, the Republican incumbent senator.

The Palmetto State has not elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1998, and Donald Trump won it by nearly 18 points in 2024, but a New York Times/Siena poll this week has the two candidates neck and neck, at 48% each.
Graham was appointed to the seat after her brother, Lindsey Graham, died in July, and she entered the race at Trump’s urging, without having ever held elected office.

Her inexperience has become one of the defining aspects of the campaign, which culminated in an August debate when she admitted she was “not that informed on national security” when asked about US policy on Taiwan. In the poll, 51% of voters said she lacked the right experience to be an effective senator.

Andrews, a pediatrician from Charleston, has meanwhile built her campaign around her medical career. Her solution to better access to doctors and climbing medical bills has been to advocate for a public option and cheaper prescription drugs.
Obama-era investigation reportedly found some evidence against Ilhan Omar's marriage

An Obama-era federal investigation of Minnesota representative Ilhan Omar found some evidence suggesting that she entered into a sham marriage in 2009 to help a man suspected of being her brother obtain a green card, according to the New York Times (paywall).
At issue is Omar’s 2009 marriage, when she was already a US citizen, to Ahmed Nur Said Elmi, a British citizen whom she divorced in 2017.

Current and former officials told the paper that the FBI and the Department of Homeland Security investigated the marriage in the summer of 2016, but the case stalled chiefly because prosecutors concluded that the suspected crime fell outside a five-year statute of limitations.
The Times notes that it remains unclear what evidence investigators had that suggested the marriage was fraudulent and that the person Omar married was her brother.
Marrying someone for the sole purpose of helping them obtain a green card is illegal under federal law, while marrying a sibling is illegal under state law.
Omar has denied the allegations. Spokesperson Jackie Rogers told the NYT in a statement:

Rep. Omar has repeatedly and unequivocally denied this baseless, disgusting conspiracy theory. This is a desperate political smear designed to distract from Trump’s failed presidency and two years of Republican failure in Congress.
Another aspect that remains unclear whether federal prosecutors could still pursue charges in spite of the statute of limitations for marriage-based immigration fraud.
The Trump administration has revisited the case as part of a wider investigation into Omar’s family’s immigration history to the United States.

Investigators are examining whether Omar’s late father lied or omitted information in immigration forms before becoming an American citizen, and whether Omar, who was a child when she immigrated to the United States, was too old to have qualified for citizenship through her father in 2000, the Times reported.
Trump’s homeland security secretary Markwayne Mullin said of the matter last month, in remarks directed at Omar:
If we can prove that you shouldn’t have been here in the first place, we’ll deport you.
Officials in the Trump administration lured automakers to expand manufacturing in the US by dangling a chance at tariff relief, according to new reporting from the Wall Street Journal.

The outlet, citing sources privy to details of the plan, reported that the Trump administration had promised Volkswagen executives that companies that invest in the US would soon benefit from a tariff relief program, before the administration unveiled a new $4bn Audi plant in Georgia. (Audi is owned by Volkswagen.)

The tariff relief program the Trump administration promised would come through the US Department of Commerce, the Journal reported. The plan, which is not yet finalized, would establish carve-outs for companies that commit to building factories in the US.
En route to Texas campaign event, Vance calls for fraud investigation into Peltola

On his way to a campaign event in Texas, JD Vance backed an investigation into Mary Peltola’s alleged scheme to siphon away votes from her Senate opponent by a recruiting a candidate with the same name.

Addressing reporters on the tarmac, Vance said that Peltola had “tried to commit election fraud” in the Alaska Senate race by recruiting a man named Dan Sullivan to run against her primary opponent, Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan.

When asked whether he agreed with Trump’s insistence that Peltola be criminally prosecuted for the tactic (which, while underhanded, has been employed elsewhere, and is not clearly illegal) Vance backed the idea, though in not in quite so strong terms.
“I think that we should certainly look into whether she committed election fraud,” Vance said.
He continued: “She is trying to steal a Senate seat from the voters of Alaska, and it’s disgraceful. So whether it’s criminal or not, she certainly has committed, I think, a great moral failing.”

While Trump is campaigning in South Carolina, Vance is heading to Texas to try and win support for Ken Paxton. Paxton, a scandal-marred former Texas attorney general and Trump devotee, has trailed in the polls in recent weeks, putting the Republicans at risk of losing a Senate seat in Texas for the first time in decades.

articles.headline: Sir Patrick Stewart passes away at 86
keyFacts: Actor Sir Patrick Stewart has passed away at the age of 86 at his home in Los Angeles.
A statement on his Instagram confirmed he had been living with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia.
The statement requested that donations be made to Alzheimer's research and caregiver charities in lieu of flowers.
body: The legendary actor, perhaps best known for his work on Star Tre k as Captain Picard, has passed away, according to a statement posted to his Instagram, which was first reported by The Hollywood Reporter . The statement also disclosed that theYorkshire-born actor had been living with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia.

Born in Mirfield, West Yorkshire, in 1940, Stewart joined the Royal Shakespeare Company at the age of 26 before becoming a household name as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation from 1987 to 1994. He later revisited the role in four feature films and the three-season Star Trek: Picard series. He also played Professor Charles Xavier in X-Men . He was knighted in 2010, and published his memoir, Making It So, in 2023.

“We announce with great sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles,” the statement reads, noting that he was “in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny” after “a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia.” It added that “He will be remembered for the dignity, compassion and humanity he brought to every role,” and asked for donations to Alzheimer’s research and caregiver charities in lieu of flowers.
In lieu of flowers, memorial contributions may be made to:
Johns Hopkins Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center Fund https://t.co/luC5CdcWDy
Alzheimer’s Foundation of America Caregiver Resources https://t.co/zvNptfyuNd
Photo Credit: Tommy Garcia pic.twitter.com/XNncEVq56X
— Patrick Stewart (@SirPatStew) October 29, 2026
The statement also quotes his memoir:

“Like me, Jean-Luc has lived an unusual life that has taken him far beyond the bounds of normal human experience. But he is also someone who has remained true to his earthbound roots, for they are what gave him his identity. In the end, he feels the call of home, as do I.”

In gaming circles, his performance as Emperor Uriel Septim VII in The Elder Scrolls IV is, of course, the standout, with Zobek in Castlevania: Lords of Shadow and the reprisal of Professor X in 2005’s X-Men Legends II: Rise of Apocalypse .

My enduring memory of the man will remain the way he approached the Ice Bucket Challenge back in August 2014, in support of ALS research: signing a check, getting a bucket of ice, adding a few cubes of ice to a glass of something nice, and drinking it with a smile to the camera. Pure class.
Godspeed, Captain.
The post Sir Patrick Stewart passes away at 86 appeared first on Destructoid .

articles.headline: DOJ ramps up criminal probe into Alaska’s ‘Decoy Dan’, preps grand jury subpoenas
keyFacts: The Justice Department escalated its Alaska Senate race probe and will issue dozens of grand jury subpoenas Thursday, sources said.
Democratic candidate Mary Peltola and campaign officials were aware of a decoy scheme, according to a report.
A DOJ official said prosecutors are exploring conspiracy charges over alleged voter rights violations.
body: WASHINGTON — The Justice Department has dramatically escalated its investigation into the Alaska Senate race and will issue dozens of new grand jury subpoenas on Thursday, according to people familiar with the matter.

The escalation comes in the wake of a damning New York Times report about the scheme, which was reported to involve Democratic campaign officials. Democratic candidate Mary Peltola was also aware of the efforts, the report said.
Prosecutors are exploring whether to bring charges alleging a conspiracy to violate voters’ rights, according to a DOJ official.

The department, at President Trump’s direction, filed a civil lawsuit last week seeking to stop the state from certifying the results of the election should Sen. Sullivan lose with a “decoy” candidate known as Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. on the ballot.

articles.headline: Everton v Newcastle: Carabao Cup fourth round – live
keyFacts: Everton secured a quarter-final match against Fleetwood Town after goals from James Garner and Hayden Hackney defeated Newcastle.
Jack Grealish was dropped from Everton's squad due to a breach of club discipline following an unauthorized absence from training.
Newcastle made three second-half substitutions, bringing on Joelinton, Elanga, and Wissa as they attempted to mount a comeback.
body: 64 min: Elanga advances down the left and looks for Murphy at the far stick. Mykolenko is forced to head behind under pressure. Hall to send this one in … but it fails to beat the first man and Schar is penalised for grabbing some blue shirt.
63 min: … Elanga slices wildly into the stand behind the goal. Poor shot, though it was also a poor punch clear by Pickford. Both players should have executed better.

62 min: Hackney clatters into the back of Hall, and suddenly the former Middlesbrough man needs to watch himself against his old north-east rivals. One more loose one and he could be in a spot of bother. The resulting free kick’s launched into the mixer, winning a corner for Newcastle, from which …

59 min: Hackney is skittled 30 yards from goal, just to the left of centre. A promising situation … but Dewsbury-Hall slams a witless free kick straight into the wall. Newcastle counter through Elanga, who is stopped in full flight by Rohl’s well-timed last-ditch challenge. Next goal feels so important … though they always do, don’t they?
58 min: Elanga wins a corner. Pickford claims it. Everton counter through Dewsbury-Hall, who nearly finds Barry six yards out with a cross from the left. Murphy heads clear.

55 min: Dedic latches onto a loose ball, the best part of 30 yards from the Everton goal. He aims a first-time drive goalwards; the ball loops off Hackney’s ankle and nearly spins into the top left. Wide and high, but it’s a corner, and though nothing comes of the set piece, Newcastle are finally applying a little bit of pressure. Everton’s fans, starved of exciting cup runs for so long, are understandably getting a bit edgy now, with so much to lose.
54 min: A simple long Willock pass down the middle nearly opens up Everton. Wissa nicks in ahead of O’Brien, but can’t get enough power on an attempted looping header over Pickford, who claims.

52 min: Elanga makes a nuisance of himself down the left and feeds Hall, who crosses deep. Murphy, from a tight angle beyond the far post, tries to volley goalwards but can’t get his effort on target. To be fair, that would have been one heck of a finish had he connected properly. It wasn’t exactly a gimme.
Newcastle, who get the second half started, have indeed sent on Joelinton. They’ve also brought on Elanga and Wissa. Osula, Barnes and Ramsey have made way.

Everton assume control of this tie with a quick one-two, and with Fleetwood Town waiting in the quarters, dreams of a march to the semi-finals may be a tad previous … but also understandable! It’s party time at the HDS.

Barnes shoots. A deflected shot is gathered by Pickford, who sends Dewsbury-Hall off on the counter. Ramsey clips Dewsbury-Hall, but the ball breaks to Barry on the left, so the referee waves play on. Barry clips the cross back into the centre, and Hackney, rushing in, opens his body to slot across Hornicek and into the bottom left!

43 min: Barnes and Osula combine at close quarters on the penalty spot. Osula goes over. No penalty. Then Barnes is clipped lightly by Tarkowski, though it’s not enough for the referee. Erm. Indistinct colours clashing, a bit like this …

41 min: Tarkowski runs the ball out of play down the left for a corner. He wears the look of a guilty man, and waits for a whistle that doesn’t come. So then he clears his lines. At least the ball looked over the line in super non-sharp lo-def … but let’s not belabour the point any more.

39 min: Some pinball in the Everton box. The ball breaks to Barnes, on the left-hand corner of the six-yard box. He drags a weak shot wide left. Newcastle have not achieved very much since falling behind.

38 min: A throw for Everton deep in Toon territory down the right. O’Brien flings it long. Some shoving. Ramsey wins a free kick and Newcastle clear their lines. “At least the teams are wearing contrasting shirts,” begins the text written on Andy (not that one) Flintoff’s subterranean bar, “so if Sky decided to go back to B/W (to save more bandwidth than they already are doing with their high picture compression) you could tell them apart.”

36 min: That’s got the Hill Dickinson bouncing. Newcastle have been the better side on balance – just about – but Everton have come up with the one moment of true quality. They’ll be heading to Fleetwood for a December quarter-final as things stand!

Out of nothing, a moment of sheer quality! Pickford goes long down the left. George gets the better of Dedic and lays off to Hackney, who shuttles further infield for Garner, who lets the ball roll across him before whistling an unstoppable shot across Hornicek and into the bottom right! Lovely goal.

32 min: Osula felt that block from Tarkowski, and he needs a little bit of treatment. He should be fine to continue, though. It’s not quite sparked, this match. “I think Jack Grealish might be onto something with his little No Show at training,” quips Chris Paraskevas.

30 min: Willock feeds Osula in the Everton box down the left. Osula shoots. Tarkowski blocks; he had to. Everton counter through Garner down the right, but with blue shirts in the middle, the resulting cross is not good.

28 min: Barry chases a loose ball. Schar gets there first and batters it straight into him. A throw is one. Pleasingly old-school, like the 405-line Marconi-EMI system used by Sky Sports the BBC in the 1930s.

26 min: Dibling drags a poor shot wide right. He had options in the middle; poor decision. “You say it’s Andy Burnham in the house but it looks like Andoni Iraola has come to curse it,” writes Ian Copestake, who doesn’t say whether he’s viewing this MBM through the Sky Sports + Zoetrope system.

25 min: George has a dig from the edge of the box. His shot is deflected and nearly drops to Hackney on the penalty spot, but the luck’s not with Everton here and Newcastle are able to toe-poke clear. The home crowd, muttering away with concern not so long ago, are vocal now.

23 min: Dibling teases Hall down the right and wins Everton their first corner of the evening. Dewsbury-Hall swings it in. Barnes larrups the dropping ball clear. A decent response from Everton, who were on the ropes for a while back there.

21 min: Mykolenko and George combine crisply down the left. A low cross comes in. Hackney meets it at the near stick with a sidefoot, but doesn’t get any purchase on the shot, which dribbles into the arms of Hornicek. That’s better from Everton, though.
18 min: Now Schar has a pop from distance. Pickford parries. Newcastle are suddenly completely on top, and there are a few murmurs coming down from the HDS stands.

16 min: Now it’s Barnes’ turn to win possession far too easily in the midfield. He slips in Willock down the left. Willock shoots from a tight angle. Pickford spills, but there’s a nearby blue smudge available to clear.

14 min: Hall wins a 40-60 in the midfield, Rohl allowing him to win a challenge he never should have won. He powers down the left and feeds Barnes, who enters the box and tees up Murphy, who can’t get a shot away. Ramsey then has a go, but Mykolenko gets in the road. Some last-ditch defending allows Everton to get away with a big one. Newcastle should have worked Pickford at the very least.

12 min: Gonzalez, quarterbacking from deep, pings a long diagonal towards Barnes, on the left-hand corner of the six-yard box. Barnes heads goalwards, but straight at Pickford, who tips around the post. Nothing comes of the resulting corner.

10 min: There’s not much of a rhythm to this game. No wonder they’ve hidden it away behind the red button on their Plus channel, eh folks, etc. To be fair, at least they’ve cleaned all the slots of their zoetrope.

6 min: Pickford goes long. Barry tries to burst clear down the inside-right channel, but Burn has a hold of him and there’s no way to wriggle into the box. I think. This is like watching a parody of 1970s iron-curtain children’s programming.

4 min: I say that about the colours: at least that’s what the indistinct shapes on the Sky coverage look like. The def is very lo. A lot of flitting in and out of focus. Allow me to adjust both my aerial and my tin hat, but I wonder if they’d treat a tie involving Manchester United, Liverpool, Arsenal or Spurs with this level of ill-defined disdain?

PM 4 EFC. Andy Burnham is in the house tonight, offering his support to his beloved Everton. He’s the first prime minister to support the club, though Harold Wilson used to frequent Goodison in the 1960s and 1970s, albeit as a Huddersfield Town fan. Newcastle United have to make do with Tony Blair, famously photographed playing keepy-uppy with Kevin Keegan back in the mid-1990s. As in so many other ways, Clem Attlee rises over Blair and Burnham like a colossus, on account of having actually played the game for non-league Fleet Town, but we’re going well off piste now.

There are only three clubs left in this season’s competition to have previously won the League Cup. Liverpool and Manchester City have 19 wins between them, Newcastle another one. Everton are one of three clubs to have at least reached the final (1977 and 1984), Sunderland (1985 and 2014) and Bradford City (2013) being the other two. Crystal Palace, Bournemouth and Fleetwood Town are yet to make it to a final. So while the door’s not quite yet at the stage of flapping wide open for some history makers to barrel through, it is at least ajar. Possibilities ahoy!
1. The winner of tonight’s tie will travel to Fleetwood Town for a quarter-final to be played the week commencing 14 December 2026.
2. There is no VAR tonight.
3. Should tonight’s tie be level after 90 minutes plus stoppages, there will be no extra time and instead the match will move straight to …
Team news: Grealish dropped due to 'breach of Club discipline'

Everton make two changes to their starting XI following last weekend’s 2-0 defeat at Arsenal. Hayden Hackney and Tyler Dibling come in for Brennan Johnson and Harrison Armstrong, who both drop to the bench. Jarrad Branthwaite is unavailable due to concussion protocols, while Jack Grealish has been dropped from the squad “due to a breach of Club discipline”, reportedly the result of an unauthorised absence from training.
Newcastle United make one change to their starting line-up following last weekend’s 2-0 win at Crystal Palace. Jacob Ramsey takes the place of Joelinton, who starts as a sub.

It wasn’t so long ago that Newcastle United were the watchword for underperforming silverware-repelling giants. But lifting the 2025 League Cup did for that. Now it’s over to Everton, a trophy-hoovering behemoth whose spree started in Victorian times only to come to a juddering and ignominious halt in 1995. It’s about time, and this campaign represents the first stirring of a cup run in a wee while, so people are beginning to talk. Fleetwood Town await the winners of this tie in the quarters, so a pathway is opening up. Is this to be Everton’s year, their first in 31? Or are Newcastle to make it a successful London-buses quest, a second pot in three years after that 56-year wait? Only one of these grand old clubs can keep it going past 10pm or so. Kick-off is at 7.45pm GMT. It’s on!

articles.headline: Justice for Maya women in Guatemala, girls back in school in India, restored land in Mali: The UN has named its 2026 SDG Action Award winners
keyFacts: The UN SDG Action Campaign announced its 2026 award winners from over 7,000 entries at a ceremony in Rome.
Groups from Guatemala, India, and Mali received awards for advancing Indigenous women's rights, girls' education, and land restoration.
The awards support the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, which target global issues such as poverty, education, and climate protection.
body: A legal aid group for Indigenous women in Guatemala, a movement of village mothers in rural India, and a Malian entrepreneur who restores farmland have won this year's UN SDG Action Awards.
The winners were announced at the ninth Heroes of Tomorrow awards ceremony in Rome, Italy, run by the UN SDG Action Campaign. They were chosen from more than 7,000 entries from 190 countries.
Nine finalists were shortlisted for three categories: resilience, creativity and changemaker.
Justice for Maya women

The Resilience Award went to the Women's Justice Initiative. Many indigenous women in Guatemala face high rates of violence, poverty and discrimination, made worse by language barriers and a lack of access to information. The initiative helps women and girls get access to justice and lead change in their communities. According to the organization, more than 16,000 women and girls have participated.

"I accept the UN SDG Action Award in the honour of the Maya Kaqchikel women and girls in Guatemala who are building a more just future for their communities. Ending violence against women requires all of us. Only together, we can build a future where every woman and girl lives with dignity and realizes her full potential," said Viviana Patal, the initiative's legal director.
Keeping girls in school in India

The Creativity Award was given to Mothers of Courage, a grassroots campaign that aims to keep girls in education in rural India. Its organizers say more than 1.2 million people have joined and pledged to keep their daughters in education and to prevent early marriage.

"This award today belongs to all the mothers in those villages, all the women leaders, who are working hard to change the destinies of their daughters and their daughters-in-law," said Khushboo Awasthi, Mothers of Courage's chief curator.
"Together, let's create a world where no girl ever has to negotiate for her right to dream and to aspire and to thrive."
Trees and livelihoods in Mali

The Changemaker Award when to Malian entrepreneur Rokiatou Traore. Her organization, Herou Alliance, helps women and small farmers bring worn-out land back to life by planting trees alongside their crops. The trees also help farmers generate extra revenue, allowing them to sell products from moringa and other valuable trees.

"Receiving this award means a lot to me. It is a reminder of why I started this journey," said Traore. "I invite you all to join us, to plant more trees, to empower more women, and above all, to create a future full of opportunities for communities for today and for future generations."

The UN Trust Fund to End Violence against Women and Girls received an honorable mention. Speaking about the award, President of the Organization of Women's Freedom in Iraq Jannat Al Ghezi paid a tearful tribute to its founder Yanar Mohammed, who was assassinated outside her home in Baghdad in March.
'Be that change'

UN Assistant Secretary-General Michelle Muschett said the finalists "remind us that the future is something we create together and that each of us has the power to help shape it and open doors for the next generations."

"When they tell you that one person cannot make a difference, prove them wrong," UN SDG Action Campaign Director Marina Ponti told the audience. "Change has always begun with people who refused to accept that the world could not be different. So be courageous. Be persistent. Be that change."
How are the awards organized?

A panel of 20 judges from UN leadership, government, civil society, the arts, business and youth activism chose the winners. They included UN Development Programme Administrator Alexander De Croo, Oxfam International Executive Director Amitabh Behar, and Otto Group Vice President Tobias Wollermann.

The awards are run by the UN SDG Action Campaign, a special initiative of the UN Secretary-General. The campaign supports the UN Sustainable Development Goals, 17 targets adopted by member states that cover areas including poverty, hunger, education, gender equality and climate protection.
The awards are supported by Italy's Foreign Ministry and Germany's Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development.
Editor's Note: DW Director General Barbara Massing was a member of the 20-person jury panel.

articles.headline: Alaska governor raises concern of ‘cover-up’ in Mary Peltola ballot scandal
keyFacts: Alaska Governor Mike Dunleavy directed an investigation into allegations that Mary Peltola's Senate campaign recruited a spoiler candidate to confuse voters.
Peltola denied the allegations, while Dunleavy said the investigation aims to protect election integrity and could lead to criminal charges.
Dunleavy criticized Alaska's ranked choice voting system for enabling the alleged scheme, which Alaskans will vote to repeal in 2026.
body: Gov. Mike Dunleavy (R-AK) said Thursday that he was concerned that Democrat Mary Peltola’s Senate campaign was engaged in a “cover-up” over its alleged scheme to prop up a spoiler candidate to confuse voters in the Alaska race.

Dunleavy spoke with Fox News after announcing his intention to open an investigation into an alleged plan to seek out a candidate with the same name as incumbent Sen. Dan Sullivan (R-AK) to siphon votes away from the Republican.

“We got to get to the bottom of this quickly because you have some actions that are taking place, but there also may be a cover-up,” Dunleavy said. “We’ll find out through our investigation. This is so unfortunate.”

The governor directed the Alaska Department of Public Safety to open an investigation into Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. after the New York Times published a report Wednesday claiming that the Peltola campaign coordinated with Democratic operatives to recruit a second Dan Sullivan to be on the Senate ballot to confuse voters. Peltola has denied the allegations that she played a hand in the Daniel J. Sullivan Jr.’s candidacy.

Dunleavy’s administration had challenged the second Sullivan’s eligibility over the summer, but the Alaska Supreme Court overturned the decision. The initial investigation, Dunleavy said, was just the beginning of the current situation.
“We saw the tip of the iceberg back in May and June, and now we’re seeing more of the iceberg, as they would say, ” he said.
Dunleavy emphasized that his intention is to protect the integrity of elections, not to target Peltola, although he noted the issues this causes for her campaign.

“This is hugely problematic for the candidate,” he said. “And again, our investigation, if it leads to criminal charges, we don’t care who that is. We don’t care if it’s a candidate, we don’t care whose name it is, because what’s more important is maintaining election integrity for the people of Alaska itself. If it leads to that individual, the candidate, then so be it.
Dunleavy also used the circumstances to criticize the state’s ranked choice voting system, which he said enabled the alleged spoiler candidate to be on the ballot.

“We would not be having this conversation at all if we didn’t have a thing in place called ranked choice voting in the state of Alaska,” he said, adding the state’s jungle primary system negatively “impacts election integrity.”
Alaska gubernatorial candidate Bernadette Wilson, who is looking to succeed Dunleavy, echoed the governor’s concerns with ranked choice voting.

“Because ranked choice voting allows the top four to go on, you now have political parties, special interest groups that are funding a candidate who they don’t even support,” Wilson said. “They don’t even support that candidate, but they’re holding them up.

“They’re manipulating this system because they know that if they can shave off 2%, 3%, maybe it’s 5%, that they shave off from the actual leading Republican candidate, then they feel like it gives their candidate a chance,” she continued. “More than anything, I think that it definitely appears as though it is quite fraudulent behavior. It is very much deceiving because of ranked choice voting.”
SEN. DAN SULLIVAN TELLS ALASKANS NOT TO RANK MARY PELTOLA BUT INCLUDE ‘DECOY DAN’ ON BALLOT

Alaska utilizes a top-four primary, in which the four highest vote-getters from the August primary advance to the general election. Voters can rank up to four candidates. The person with the fewest votes after each round is eliminated, with ballots reapportioned or exhausted until the winner clears 50%.

In the 2026 elections, Alaskans are voting on a ballot measure to repeal ranked choice voting. President Donald Trump has expressed his displeasure with the system on multiple occasions and encouraged the state to vote “yes” to move away from the system.

articles.headline: Ubisoft Issues Official Update on Fate of Future Assassin's Creed Remakes
keyFacts: Ubisoft announced on Thursday that the company currently has no other Assassin's Creed remakes actively in development.
Ubisoft stated that its teams are focused on upcoming franchise projects, including the multiplayer game Invictus and Codename Hexe.
Ubisoft stated that the company remains open to exploring opportunities for more remakes or rereleases in the future.
body: Ubisoft's latest Assassin's Creed game was a blast from the past. Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced is a remake of the 2013 pirate adventure. As remakes become more and more common in the industry, fans have naturally wondered if more Assassin's Creed remakes are in the pipeline. In 2024, CEO Yves Guillemot hinted at such, saying, "Players can be excited about some remakes, which will allow us to revisit some of the games we've created in the past and modernize them."
His use of the plural "remakes" hinted at remakes other than just Black Flag Resynced, but Ubisoft has now confirmed the status of other Assassin's Creed games under active development.

On Thursday, Ubisoft updated fans on the status of the franchise, and touched on fan demand for additional remakes. "One thing we want to be transparent about today is that we currently have no other Assassin's Creed remake actively in development," Ubisoft said. "Our teams are already focused on the next chapter of Assassin's Creed titles, including projects you haven't heard about yet, featuring new settings and stories."

However, just because they're not actively being worked on, don't rule out the possibility of more remakes, or rereleases, sometime in the future. "Like many of you, we love the idea of revisiting our classic titles, and we'll keep exploring opportunities to bring older titles back. That door remains open because, after all... Nothing is true, everything is permitted," Ubisoft said, referencing the oft-repeated Assassin maxim.
What does the next chapter of Assassin's Creed look like?

Ubisoft has several Assassin's Creed games in the works. Assassin’s Creed Invictus, the PvP multiplayer game, recently had a private playtest where hundreds of players got to check it out. "The response to the return of PvP multiplayer was very positive," Ubisoft said. It noted that players "wanted more of the pillars that define Assassin's Creed" in Invictus, and the development team has been working for months acting on that feedback.

Codename Hexe is also in the works, but Ubisoft was a little quieter about that game. It's "making steady progress on this darker" project, though Ubisoft won't share a major update on it until some time in 2027. In the Codename Hexe section, Ubisoft also shared some sort of cryptic message without context:
ZKLWAVN MBEXNK ULYCNJ... LWY01... I#########F
// QNTMAKHX TWTEMZL. YSIZKQ AADSWX NFAAMPHP.//

No idea what that means! But surely the fans will have their theories. Next year marks 20 years of Assassin's Creed, and Ubisoft will share more of how it intends to celebrate the milestone in the coming months.

articles.headline: Where To Find All Serpent Houses In Phantom Blade Zero
keyFacts: Visiting the Serpent Houses in Phantom Blade Zero is required to progress to the late-game stages of the campaign.
Players can find the Green Serpent House, Red Serpent House, Black Serpent House, and White Serpent House across different regions.
Placing the three quest items into the ornate door in the Green Serpent House opens a passageway leading to the Mirage Estate.
body: Are you looking for the Serpent Houses in Phantom Blade Zero ? It’s imperative that you visit these locations while exploring, as doing so allows you to progress to the late-game stages of the campaign. We’ve got all the details for you in this article, but be ready for a few minor spoilers in the sections below.
Pangzhen: Green Serpent House

The Green Serpent House is practically unmissable, since you head there while tackling main quest objectives in Pangzhen. The apprentice, Xie Xaorong, unlocks the medicine upgrade function at bells. He tells you that the ornate snake door is locked, as it’s missing the eyes, tongue, and fang.
This location also nets you the following goodies:
Green Serpent Brew (medicine)
Serpent Gall: Green (fragment)
This fella has a few tips for ya.
Crimson Forest: Red Serpent House

This Phantom Blade Zero Serpent House will likely be the first that you stumble upon in the campaign. It’s due north of the Thieves’ Camp, but you’ll only be able to enter it once you have the Flaming Mane. The Phantom Edge comes from the Lion Dance Grandmaster boss in northwest Pangzhen, so just do the main quest objectives there until you obtain it.
The Flaming Mane is used to burn the brambles in this area. Once you’re inside, pick up the loot, including:
Red Serpent Tongue (quest item)
Loong Emblem: Yin (quest item)
Serpent Rattle: Red (fragment)
Revisit the Crimson Forest to enter the Red Serpent House.
Village of Lu: Black Serpent House
Next, use the Flaming Mane to torch the brambles in the Village of Lu and grab the following in the den:
Black Serpent Fang (quest item)
Loong Emblem: Yang (quest item)
Serpent Venom Sac: Black (fragment)
Reinforced Bowstring (Soul Temper - Feather Bow)
Return to the Village of Lu for the Black Serpent House.
Meigu Lake: White Serpent House

The Lóng Emblems that you’ve collected are needed for the Serpent House in Phantom Blade Zero. The den is on an island at the eastern part of the lake, and the emblems can unlock the main area. You’ll find the following items there:
Treasure Basin (accessory) - Inside the small building to the right.
Sha-Chi Amber Fragment (upgrade) - Go to the back of said building.
Serpent Slough: White (fragment)
Sundering Dual Axes (dual-wield weapon) - Dropped by Heartpiercer, Elite Shadow Warden.
White Serpent Eye (quest item)
2x Leng Tu’s Memory Flowers
Note: The four fragments that you’ve collected are automatically combined to create the Serpent’s Memory, a Soul Temper material for the White Serpent & Crimson Viper.
Sail across Meigu Lake and gain access to the White Serpent House.
The Serpent Door and the Mirage Estate - Point of no return

You can place the three quest items--Red Serpent Tongue, Black Serpent Fang, and White Serpent Eye--in the ornate door in Pangzhen’s Green Serpent House. Doing so opens a hidden passageway that leads to the Mirage Estate.

To be clear, this is a point of no return. When you go through the passageway, you’ll receive a warning telling you that you still have “unfinished business.” If you proceed further, you’ll arrive at the Mirage Estate, though it’s possible that several quests will also fail abruptly. That’s why it’s important to tackle key objectives before you proceed.

In any case, that does it for our guide on where to find all Serpent Houses in Phantom Blade Zero. At this stage, we encourage you to thoroughly explore other regions. You can gather more main weapons and their respective Soul Temper materials .
Join Soul as he faces numerous threats in the Wulin and be sure to check out more tips in our Phantom Blade Zero guides hub .

articles.headline: Dem probes could ‘torture’ young Trump officials with crushing legal bills, subpoenaed conservative warns
keyFacts: Conservative leader Rachel Bovard warned Democratic investigations could inflict heavy legal costs and reputational damage on young Trump administration officials.
Senator Elissa Slotkin stated she wants Democrats to target people who enabled Donald Trump to send a deterrence message to prospective staff.
Donald Trump told Time magazine he would issue preemptive pardons to administration members before leaving office to protect them from legal exposure.
body: Repeated calls by Democratic lawmakers to investigate President Donald Trump and his allies are raising concerns from a conservative organization previously subpoenaed during former Biden-appointed special counsel Jack Smith’s 2020 election investigation.
And one of its leaders is warning that young professionals could face reputational damage and steep legal bills.

Rachel Bovard, vice president of programs at the Conservative Partnership Institute (CPI), said Smith's investigation left her organization on the hook for millions of dollars in fees to ensure compliance with the subpoenas.
HOUSE DEMS PLOT TRUMP INVESTIGATION BLITZ IF THEY SEIZE MAJORITY

"Jack Smith was a test run in how to do this," Bovard told Fox News Digital. "Jack Smith basically went in crazy, subpoenaed a host of information across the right. His goal was to map the right, and he did it. And all of that information is still on file at the FBI and the Justice Department. It doesn't go away, so it's sitting there waiting for the next Dem administration to pick it up, and we expect that's what they'll do with it."

Though CPI was targeted by the Biden Justice Department and not Congress, Bovard said she fears Democrats will follow what she described as Smith's playbook if they win control of Congress in the midterm elections.

The concerns come after Sen. Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., stated during an event earlier this month at the University of Chicago's Institute of Politics that she wants Democrats to send a "deterrence message" to any young person considering working in the Trump administration. Slotkin said she wants to "not just focus on the president, but on the people who enabled him."

"They literally just want to use the government as a political weapon, which is exactly what Jack Smith also did to a bunch of people, including my organization," Bovard told Fox News Digital. "We were never credibly accused of any crime, but we had to spend millions of dollars to comply with subpoenas."
Bovard said Smith's subpoenas allowed the Justice Department to obtain detailed information such as CPI's health coverage and benefits, which she said had no relevance to Smith's investigation.
Fox News Digital reached out to Slotkin's office for comment but did not receive a response before publication.

Abhishek Kambli, a former federal prosecutor and a partner at Holtzman Vogel, told Fox News Digital that Congress' ability to issue subpoenas and conduct investigations must be related to legislative duties and that Congress can't issue subpoenas for law enforcement purposes. Kambli said remarks by Slotkin and other members of Congress could be used as evidence by anyone seeking to challenge a subpoena.
"You had multiple members of the House and the Senate that talk about the accountability agenda and holding the Trump administration accountable for wrongdoing," Kambli told Fox News Digital.
"And if they just throw in boilerplate language that this is for legislative purpose, anyone challenging those subpoenas will have that entire record to demonstrate that it's anything but that."

While Michael Morley, a law professor at Florida State University College of Law, agreed that Slotkin's remarks are bad optics, he said Congress' authority to conduct investigations is still broad, pointing out that Congress can investigate the agencies it has created.

"I don't think that is consistent with our norms, and I certainly don't think it's something that we'd like to see become a routine part of our discourse," Morley said of Slotkin's remarks. "But I don't think that necessarily means it rises to the level of a constitutional issue."
ELISSA SLOTKIN CALLS BACKLASH TO THREAT OF PROSECUTION COMMENTS 'MANUFACTURED OUTRAGE'

Hans von Spakovsky, a senior legal fellow at Advancing American Freedom, said that while Congress may be able to hold someone in criminal contempt for not complying with a subpoena, it's up to the Justice Department to prosecute, which it could decline to do.

Spakovsky said that precedent was established during the Obama administration, when the Justice Department declined to prosecute then-Attorney General Eric Holder after the House held him in contempt for refusing to comply with a subpoena related to the Fast and Furious investigation.
But Kambli said that doesn't erase the risks potential Trump administration officials could face, arguing that the investigative process itself can be the punishment.

"There is no doubt that some members of Congress intend to use that process to bankrupt people who cannot afford legal representation," Kambli told Fox News Digital. "That is a real threat, regardless of whether anyone is ultimately prosecuted."
SLOTKIN'S VIRAL 'THREAT' TO CONSERVATIVES TAKES NEW TWIST AS STUDENT MOVES TO HOLD HER ACCOUNTABLE: 'SHOCKING'
Bovard said when she first saw Slotkin's remarks about seeking a "deterrence message" she interpreted them as a call to use the investigative process to "torture" young professionals.
"I don't know that these Democrats think they can actually put people in jail. I think that's almost beside the point for them," Bovard told Fox News Digital.
Kambli said concerns remain that if a Democrat returns to the White House, former Trump administration officials could be subjected to Justice Department investigations.
"Where the real exposure lies is in the scenario where a Democrat wins the presidency in 2028, and they maintain both houses of Congress," Kambli told Fox News Digital.

Just weeks before Slotkin's remarks, Trump said during an interview with Time magazine that he would issue preemptive pardons to members of his administration before leaving the White House, pointing out that President Joe Biden issued a pardon for Dr. Anthony Fauci.
Bovard said it was unfortunate that political affairs had reached a point where mass pardons were even under consideration, but she argued they made sense given the rise in lawfare.
SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

"This is how we're going to have to live: mass pardons of your political parties on either side, and that's obviously a terrible outcome. But if, you know, the Slotkin theory is put to the test. I don't think Trump's going to have a choice. I think he's going to have to do that," Bovard told Fox News Digital.

articles.headline: Patrick Stewart, Star Trek and Shakespeare legend, has died
keyFacts: Actor Patrick Stewart has died at age 86 following a brief journey with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia, according to his official X account.
Stewart achieved international fame for his roles as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation and Professor Charles Xavier in X-Men.
Fellow actor William Shatner shared a message of condolence on X, calling Stewart a friend, a colleague, and a magnificent actor.
body: Patrick Stewart, the classically-trained actor who gained worldwide fame in the 1980s as Captain Jean-Luc Picard on Star Trek: The Next Generation and later as Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men film series, has died. A message posted on Stewart's official X account said his passing came "following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia."

Stewart joined the Royal Shakespeare Company in 1966, and took his first television role a year later on the long-running British series Coronation Street. He debuted on Broadway in 1971, and subsequently appeared in several feature films. He was knighted by Queen Elizabeth II in 2010, becoming Sir Patrick, which he described as "an unlooked-for honour."

But it was his tenure as Captain Jean-Luc Picard on Star Trek: The Next Generation that propelled him to international fame. Where his predecessor, Captain James T. Kirk, was a notorious ladies' man of action and fisticuffs, Picard brought a decidedly more intellectual and thoughtful bent to the big chair that ultimately proved one of the show's most enduring characteristics.
Once or twice, the show even allowed him to stretch his Shakespearean legs:

At the same time, there was never any question that Picard could kick whatever ass was necessary whenever it was called for, and he carried that demeanor over to his portrayal of Professor X: A kind, patient father figure of immeasurable power, whose leadership was paramount despite his gentle nature.
He also famously kicked ass in Excalibur:
And Dune:
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Stewart also accrued a number of videogame credits over the years in various Star Trek and X-Men games but others as well: He narrated Lands of Lore: The Throne of Chaos, portrayed Khelben Arunsen in Forgotten Realms: Demon Stone, and maybe most famously gave his deep, sonorous voice to Uriel Septim VII in The Elder Scrolls 4: Oblivion.
William Shatner, who played Captain Kirk on the original Star Trek series, shared a heartfelt message of condolence on X, calling Stewart "a friend, a colleague, and a magnificent actor."

"He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter, and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all," the announcement reads. "We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace."
Sir Patrick Stewart was 86.

articles.headline: Reddit will force users to log in as AI is killing search traffic
keyFacts: Reddit will require users to log in or have an account to view platform content, CEO Steve Huffman announced.

body: Reddit will force users to log in as AI is killing search traffic
The company is starting with tests outside of the US.

Reddit will no longer allow logged out users or those without an account to view content on its platform, CEO Steve Huffman shared in an update. The change, which the company said will initially be tested in "select markets" outside the US, comes as the company says that search traffic has declined significantly.

"A key piece of work to retain new audiences is shifting Reddit to a logged-in-only experience," Huffman wrote in a shareholder letter. "Moving to primarily logged-in will ensure our users have the best Reddit experience possible, and can find the content and communities most relevant to them."

The change is the most dramatic shift the company has made as it battles AI scraping and changes to internet search. It will also likely rattle users, some of whom are already frustrated with recent moves like restrictions on Old Reddit. Huffman said that it was a "big change" but necessary for the company.

"It is better for our business because we will have more signals for ads targeting, and being logged-in leads to higher engagement generally," he wrote. "It also allows us to protect access to Reddit's extremely valuable corpus of data, and helps us better adapt to emerging regulations around the world."
